Yes—you should be able to spot the Moon.

It is very high in the sky, at about **58° altitude** and **azimuth 193°**—almost due south, a little west of south. At **42% illumination**, it has a substantial bright crescent/half-moon-like portion, and its angular separation from the Sun is about **81°**, so it is well clear of the Sun rather than lost in the glare immediately around it.

The main challenge is the bright daytime sky. Look toward the south, roughly halfway between the horizon and overhead, and use the Moon’s position rather than expecting it to be obvious at first. Avoid looking anywhere near the Sun; shade your eyes or use a building/tree to block direct sunlight. Given the clear sky, its high altitude, and its fairly large illuminated fraction, an ordinary observer should have a good chance of seeing it unaided—possibly after a short search.
